notes:
Four walkthrough bullets, five steps. The walkthrough has a hole in it: bullet 2 walks you all the way to the Cloister of Frost and bullet 3 jumps straight to 'Defeat Shiva Prime', with nothing in between about how the battlefield is entered. The header's own Description says it -- 'Ring the tuning fork of ice upon the protocrystal' -- so step 3 is a trade of the fork to the Protocrystal, and it is the one step here not backed by a numbered bullet (source_bullets is empty and flagged). This is the same shape the sibling quest Class Reunion already uses for its Ice Pendulum, and the page names the protocrystal, so nothing is invented; it is only sourced from the header rather than the walkthrough.

Evidence is clean and non-overlapping: the Tuning fork of ice is granted by talking to Gulmama, so it is step 1's; the Whisper of frost drops from the fight, so it is step 4's. The fork is then step 3's items and the whisper step 5's items -- holding is not the same as having obtained it at that step, so neither breaks the duplicate-evidence rule.

Bullet 1's advice about her text changing is a fame check, not a step -- and the page is explicit that receiving the key item is what tells you the quest actually took, which is exactly what step 1's evidence encodes. The whole 'Notes' sibling section is party size, per-member forks, the 30 minute limit, the one-reward-at-a-time rule, an Earth-day cooldown, the Mini Fork of Ice shortcut and a suggestion to hold the whisper back for The Moonlit Path. None of them is a step. The empty [TABLE] and the Trust warning are noise.

STAGE D: no step or evidence altered, but the quest drops to medium. Step 3 is a rung the walkthrough does not contain -- it is patched in from the header Description -- and that same Description puts the protocrystal 'in Fei'Yin' while the step is filed under Cloister of Frost. The zone is right in game (the Cloister is what the (I-5) entrance opens into) but the page never says so, and a ladder with a hole patched from the infobox is an incomplete page by the guide's own definition. Re-checked and left alone: both key items are obtained at the step that carries them, neither is in the Reward list (Pact with Shiva, Shiva's Claws, Ice Belt, Ice Ring, Rust 'B' Gone, gil), the fork being step 3's items and the whisper step 5's items does not make either evidence twice, bullet order is the page's order, and every name -- Gulmama, Cloister of Frost, Protocrystal, Shiva Prime -- appears in the page text and resolves. The Notes section is party size, forks, the time limit, the reward choice, the Earth-day cooldown, the Mini Fork shortcut and The Moonlit Path: none are steps.

notes:
The walkthrough starts one action late. Bullet 1 is already the second thing you do -- nothing anywhere in the numbered list speaks to Lehko Habhoka, even though the header names him as the giver and the Description says he 'has summoned you to Heavens Tower'. Step 1 is therefore reconstructed from the header with an empty source_bullets. That matters more than it looks: the runtime treats accepting the quest as proof step 1 is done, so had Dhea Prandoleh been made step 1 she would have been marked complete the instant the quest opened and the ladder would have jumped straight to Velda-Galda.

Bullet 1 gives two grids and no zone. Both NPCs are placed in Windurst Waters (S) -- the page's own category list is 'Windurst Waters (S) Quests', the giver is there, and bullet 2 is the first thing that sends you anywhere else ('Head to Fort Karugo-Narugo (S)'). Flagged rather than assumed silently.

Bullets 5 and 6 are two examinations of the SAME Sunken Hollow back to back -- one cutscene, then the BCNM -- so they are one rung, the way Divine Might's Blank Target is. The Succulent dragon fruit is carried as that step's items because the page's own failure note says you need another one to re-enter; it is step 5's evidence because that is where the cactus hands it over, and the once-per-game-day limit on getting a replacement is invisible to the addon.

Bullet 7's sub-bullets are escort tactics -- the daughter's pathing, the Yagudo NINs, the exit at (G-9) on map 2 -- and bullet 8 is where the BCNM spits you out, an outcome, not a step. Bullet 9 is a real step: zoning back in is what triggers the closing cutscene and the reward.

STAGE D: ladder kept as read, quest to medium. Two independent inferences hold it up -- step 1 exists only because the header names Lehko Habhoka (no bullet speaks to him), and the zone on steps 2 and 3 comes from the page's category list, not from bullet 1, which gives two grids and no zone at all. Both are already flagged; the confidence should have said so too. Everything attacked and left standing: the Succulent dragon fruit is obtained at step 5 and merely held at step 7, so it is not evidence twice; it is not the Reward (Kitty Rod); bullet 2 crosses zones mid-sentence and the examine correctly lands in Fort Karugo-Narugo (S); bullets 5 and 6 really are the same Sunken Hollow back to back; bullet 7's escort names no monster, so mobs stays empty; bullet 8 is where the BCNM drops you, an outcome, and is carried only as a source bullet.

Bullets 1, 2 and 3 are one rung between them: go to the coffer, open it, and receive the gauntlets. The coffer is the only step in this quest with a genuine OR, and it is expressible for once -- Item Reqs names both halves, so the Davoi Coffer Key is items and the Thief's Tools are items_alt rather than a vague items_partial. Both resolve.

Adding them would hang optional rungs off the end of a quest that has already closed.

Old gauntlets and Shadow flames are the shared key items of the whole Borghertz family; within this quest each is used once, so the duplicate-evidence rule holds.

notes:
Twelve bullets plus two unnumbered lines, and one of the unnumbered lines is a real step: 'Return to the Colossal Footprint at (I-7) for a cutscene to turn in your Key Items' sits between bullets 8 and 9 with no number of its own. It is step 9 here, with an empty source_bullets, and it carries the three fished key items as an AND-list so the rung goes ready only when all three are in hand.

Bullets 6, 7 and 8 are three fishing spots for three different key items and nothing in the page orders them, so they share a group and all three draw at once. Each keeps its own evidence -- Paladin lobster, Scutum crab, Lance fish are distinct, so the duplicate rule is untouched -- and none of the ponds is named, so all three targets are none rather than a made-up 'pond'. The sub-bullet claiming you can 'fish up all 3 KI at the ocean' is a route the schema cannot express at all; it is flagged, not modelled.

The Goliath Worm is NOT a key item despite the page saying 'may not receive the KI' -- the resolver returns an ordinary item id for it and nothing in the key item table. It is bait, so it is step 5's evidence at count 3 (the page says at least three) and each fishing step's items at count 1. The fishing rod is Item Reqs 'Any fishing rod', a category and not a name, which is why the three fishing steps set items_partial.

Bullets 10, 11 and 12 are three examinations of the same Compressed Snow with a fight in the middle. 10 and 11 merge -- consecutive, same object, the second spawns the NM -- then the fight, then the third examination that closes the quest. The sub-sub-bullet about ilevel 119 being trivial is chat, not a step.

The lead-in note is two gates the addon cannot see: you must be on the Wings of the Goddess mission Fate in Haze, and you must have zoned and waited a game day since Bonds That Never Die. Both are flagged and gate nothing. The Charred Firewood gets no grid of its own -- 'two levels above and immediately north of the (I-7) tower' is an elevation, not a coordinate -- so its grid is null rather than a misleading I-7.

notes:
The Samurai twin of Borghertz's Sneaky Hands, same page skeleton with the coffer moved to Kuftal Tunnel and the key changed. 'Level: 50+ Samurai' is level 50 plus jobs ['SAM']; 'Repeatable: af' means false.

One real difference from the Thief page and it is worth flagging: this page never writes 'Treasure Coffer'. Bullet 2 says only 'Coffers spawn at ...' and bullet 3 'the coffer'. The name here is completed to the standard entity, which the sister page does spell out in full, and it is flagged target_name_inferred so a human can overrule it. The alternative was a null target and no marker at all for the one step in this quest that has a physical location worth pointing at. Bullet 2's ten spawn points live in the note -- they are one wandering coffer, not ten rungs.

The key-or-lockpick branch is expressible because Item Reqs names both sides: Kuftal Coffer Key as items, Thief's Tools as items_alt. Bullet 6 is the first-artifact-quest detour, conditional, so both its steps are optional. Bullets 7+8 merge into the Port Jeuno ???; 9+10 merge into the torch that spawns Dark Spark; bullet 11 splits into the kill and the second torch examination that yields the Shadow flames. Bullet 12 ends on the ??? with a cutscene, so it is an examine and not a turnin -- there is nobody to hand anything to.

'Two Additional Coffers' is not steps: the Temple of Uggalepih and Quicksand Caves coffers hold the body and legs, the section says they are not required, and by the time you could open them the quest is already complete.

STAGE D: step 2's target nulled. 'Treasure Coffer' appears nowhere in THIS page; the draft says so itself and completes the name from the sister page. Hard rule 1 admits no exception for an entity another page happens to spell out -- 'the coffer' is the same shape as the guide's own 'the baskets' -- so the name goes and the rung stays, which costs a marker and holds it back to Guslam rather than pointing it at a name the source never gave. Quest to medium for the same reason; target_name_inferred is left on the quest so a human can restore it deliberately. Everything else survived: 50+ Samurai is level 50 AND jobs ['SAM'], 'af' is false, Item Reqs names both sides of the key-or-lockpick branch so items/items_alt is honest, bullet 6's two actions are conditional and stay optional, bullet 11 really is a fight and an examine, and Old gauntlets and Shadow flames are each evidence exactly once and neither is the Reward (Myochin Kote).

notes:
A clean errand ladder with one trap at the end. Bullets 1 to 5 are four cities in a fixed order and each is a named, markable NPC; the only observable in the whole quest is the Jar of reversion dust from Chamama, so it is step 4's evidence and nothing else has any.

Chamama is on the 'Windurst Waters north map', which is not a zone: Windurst Waters (North) and (South) are both zone 238, Windurst Waters, and that is what is recorded.

Bullet 5's sub-bullet holds three ??? examinations in a fixed order -- (J-9), then (I-5), then the one in the pool at (J-9) that pops the Illusory Pot and your Fellow. A ??? can never carry a marker and none of the three is observable, so three rungs the player cannot be tracked through would be pure noise; they are merged into one step with the order in the note, the way the pilot merged its seven. The Signal Pearl is that step's items because the page tells you outright to have it on you.

Bullet 6 is two more unmarkable actions after the fight -- speak to your Adventuring Fellow, then examine the ??? -- and the Fellow is not a standing entity in any case: it wears the player's own fellow name, so a target of 'Adventuring Fellow' would fold to a key that can never match anything live. Both are folded into the final examine, whose note keeps the order.

The rewards table and the prose under it are about teaching your Fellow jobs with Tactics Manuals, not steps. Bullets 7, 8 and 9 are literally cutscene DIALOGUE -- three lines spoken by the Fellow and Luto -- rendered as top-level bullets because of the wiki's list markup. A verb-scanner would have made three steps out of them.

'Quest Reqs: Familiarity Level 65 or higher' has no slot in the schema and nothing in the packets reports Fellow familiarity, so it is flagged and gates nothing. Fame 'J' is Jeuno.
